<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark">
  <title>0</title>
  <link rel="icon" href="data:,">
  <style>
    *, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }
    html { -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; text-size-adjust: 100%; }
    body {
      margin: 0 auto;
      max-width: 65ch;
      padding: 1rem;
      font-family: system-ui, sans-serif;
      line-height: 1.5;
    }
    input, button, textarea, select { font: inherit; }
    h1, h2, h3 { line-height: 1.2; text-wrap: balance; }
    p { text-wrap: pretty; }
    p, li, h1, h2, h3 { overflow-wrap: break-word; }
    img, svg, video { max-width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; }
    :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid currentColor; outline-offset: 2px; }
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
      *, *::before, *::after { animation-duration: 0.01ms !important; animation-iteration-count: 1 !important; transition-duration: 0.01ms !important; scroll-behavior: auto !important; }
    }
  </style>
</head>
<body>

</body>
</html>

`0.html` is an empty starter page. The boilerplate is already solid: it has the viewport and color-scheme meta tags, a readable width limit, balanced heading wrapping, focus styles and reduced-motion handling. Nothing there really needs fixing. What would help most depends on what the page is for.

Some small template tweaks I could make:
- **`<title>`:** "0" is a placeholder, so give it a real title and add a `<meta name="description">`.
- **Skip link:** add a "skip to content" link that targets `<main id="main">`.
- **Media:** add `font-size-adjust`, and set `img { font-style: italic }` so alt text looks different when an image fails to load.
- **Dark mode:** define light and dark colours with `light-dark()` custom properties instead of relying only on the browser defaults.

Or, if you tell me what the page should contain (a landing page, an article or a tool), I can build out the `<main>` content. Which would you like?
